newsitem.title: USA: Transitional delays on Vencor offer.
newsitem.headline: Transitional delays on Vencor offer.

text.p: Transitional Hospitals Corp. Monday said its board has not yet taken a position on Vencor Inc.'s tender offer of $16 a share, or $639 million, which came after the company had agreed to merge with Select Medical Corp.
Transitional said it is trying to preserve Select's $14-per-share deal while simultaneously exploring the possibility of accepting the higher offer from Vencor.

Transitional said in a letter to shareholders it might be forced to pay a $19.4 million termination fee to Select, a privately held company based in Mechanicsburg, Pa., if it accepts the Vencor offer.
Other complications with the competing offer involve potential antitrust issues related to the termination fee, Transitional said.
Vencor, which operates long-term care hospitals, has initiated court proceedings to invalidate the termination fee, Transitional said.

Transitional, based in Las Vegas, also said it postponed the "distribution date" under its stockholder rights plan until June 3 or the date a company acquires 15 percent of its outstanding common stock, whichever is earlier.
Transitional's stock fell 12.5 cents to $15.375, while Vencor was unchanged at $38.875 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
